name: Cleveland Public Library — history facts
description: Five questions built from Cleveland Public Library's own published history, matching the sourced facts used on the /learn sample site's library dashboard. Each fact was checked against a source before being turned into a question, not recalled from memory.

source.name: cpl.org ("From Humble Beginnings", Special Collections) and the Encyclopedia of Cleveland History, case.edu
source.licence: Facts restated in original wording; not a copy of the source text.

items.question: In what year did Cleveland Public Library first open?
items.explain: It opened February 17, 1869, with about 5,800 books.

items.question: What nickname did Cleveland Public Library earn for being one of the first large libraries to let patrons pick their own books off the shelf?
items.explain: The open-shelf system, under librarian William Howard Brett, became a model for other libraries nationally.

items.question: The firm Walker & Weeks designed Main Library's current building, which opened in what year?
items.explain: The building has since been joined by the newer Louis Stokes Wing, home to TechCentral.

items.question: The John G. White Collection at Cleveland Public Library began in 1884 with a donation of how many maps?
items.explain: The collection has since grown to more than 161,000 maps and atlases.

items.question: Besides Main Library, how many branch libraries does Cleveland Public Library operate?
items.explain: The system also includes the Ohio Library for the Blind and Print Disabled.
